cita: Chen et al. (2026). MemPrivacy: Privacy-Preserving Personalized Memory Management for Edge-Cloud Agents.
problema: Cloud-assisted personalized memory for edge-cloud agents exposes sensitive user information (PII, health, credentials), while existing masking-based privacy protections destroy the semantic cues memory formation/retrieval needs, degrading personalization utility.
mecanismo: A lightweight on-device model detects privacy spans and classifies them under a four-level taxonomy (PL1 low-sensitivity ... PL4 credentials/secrets); detected spans are replaced with semantically typed placeholders (e.g. <Health_Info_1>) before anything leaves the device, the original-to-placeholder mapping is kept in a local secure DB for cross-session consistency, and the cloud response is restored locally by placeholder lookup+replace -- decoupling privacy protection from semantic destruction.
evaluacion: MemPrivacy-Bench: 200 synthetic user profiles, 155k+ privacy instances, 7 high-level/23 fine-grained scenario categories, multi-turn dialogues with direct+indirect privacy disclosure; span-extraction performance compared against GPT-5.2 and Gemini-3.1-Pro, and utility loss compared against baseline masking strategies across multiple memory systems.
numeros_clave: 200 users, 155k+ privacy instances; on-device models from 0.6B-4B parameters; utility loss limited to within 1.6% across memory systems (vs baseline masking); surpasses GPT-5.2/Gemini-3.1-Pro on privacy-span extraction while reducing inference latency.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: Edge-side privacy-span detection + typed-placeholder substitution before any cloud write (S4.1, Stage 1) is a concrete discretionary write-trigger pattern MF could adopt: type/redact sensitive spans before a fact is admitted into shared memory, not after.

A protection layer inserted before storage/retrieval keeps utility loss under 1.6% while reducing inference latency (abstract, S4.3), supporting MF's context-economy framing that write-time guard rails need not be expensive.

notes: Four-level PL1-PL4 taxonomy defined in S4.2; MemPrivacy-Bench construction in S4.3. No membership doubt.

cita: Ravindran (2026). Portable Agent Memory: A Protocol for Provenance-Verified Memory Transfer Across Heterogeneous LLM Agents.
problema: Agent memory accumulated in one vendor/model runtime is locked in, causing catastrophic knowledge loss on provider switch, with no integrity verification of transferred memory and no defense against memory-mediated prompt injection when re-hydrating memory into a different model.
mecanismo: A five-component memory model M=(E,S,P,W,I) (episodic/semantic/procedural/working/identity) is serialized into a Merkle-DAG artifact with per-entry BLAKE3 content-addressed IDs and Ed25519 root signing for tamper evidence; capability-scoped access tokens gate read/derive/export permissions per component; re-hydration runs a 7-stage pipeline (verify->filter->rank->compress->format->frame->inject) using a weighted relevance function over recency/salience/similarity/depth, then structural framing + content escaping to resist injection from recalled memory.
evaluacion: Pilot study across Claude-3.5-Sonnet/GPT-4-Turbo/Gemini-1.5-Pro (3 model-pair transfers x 3 task categories, N=50 tasks) measuring Transfer Continuity Score (TCS) and Re-Hydration Fidelity (RHF) under compression, plus a security evaluation (1,000 tamper-mutation trials, 200 injection-pattern attempts, token-validation tests) and format-efficiency/latency micro-benchmarks; Python SDK with 54 passing tests.
numeros_clave: TCS 0.83-0.92 (structured transfer) vs 0.28-0.45 no-memory baseline (2.4x mean improvement, Table 3); RHF degrades from 0.91 at 100% token budget to 0.71 at 25% (Table 4); 100% tamper-detection over 1,000 mutation trials; 0/200 injection attacks executed (Table 5); 69% storage reduction vs raw logs (89KB vs 284KB, Table 6), plus 31% more with CBOR; full re-hydration pipeline <13ms (Table 7).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The Working (W) component of M=(E,S,P,W,I) (S3.1) models transient goals/subgoals/pending actions as a first-class, content-addressed memory component -- directly transferable to MF's plan-state-as-memory need, though planning tasks show the most transfer degradation (TCS 0.81-0.85 vs 0.28 baseline, Table 3).

Merkle-DAG provenance + Ed25519 signing gives 100% tamper-detection over 1,000/1,000 mutation trials (S5.3), confirming that a cryptographic-provenance approach to fidelity/staleness is measurably enforceable at negligible cost.

Serialize/verify/re-hydrate latencies stay under 13ms (Table 7) and structured storage cuts size 69% vs raw conversation logs (Table 6), supporting MF's context-economy framing that typed memory representations are cheaper as well as safer.

notes: Pilot-scale study explicitly framed as directional (N=50 tasks, S5.1 footnote); gap analysis Table 1 positions it against MemGPT/Mem0/Zep/AMCP/Soul Protocol.

cita: Ouyang et al. (2026). MemLineage: Lineage-Guided Enforcement for LLM Agent Memory.
problema: Signature-only memory-integrity layers verify who wrote an entry but not what untrusted ancestry it was derived from, so an adversary can plant ingredients in untrusted sources and let the agent's own retrieval+summarization loop launder them into an authentic, signed entry that later justifies a sensitive action.
mecanismo: Six modules around one memory store: per-principal Ed25519 signing (M2) plus an RFC 6962 Merkle log (M3) give write-side provenance; a weighted derivation DAG (M4) records which retrieved parents influenced each new entry, propagated by a max-of-strong-edges rule trust(c)=max_p[1(w(p,c)>tau)*trust(p)] that provably preserves an Untrusted-Path label across any chain whose edges stay above threshold tau (Theorem 1); a verifier-aware retrieval hook (M5) tags trust labels at read time and a sensitive-action gate (M6) refuses tool dispatch whose justifying context descends from an External ancestor above tau.
evaluacion: Deterministic mechanism-isolation harness comparing 3 defense cells (no_defense, sig_only_baseline, MemLineage) against 3 attack families (backdoor poisoning, query-injection/retrieval poisoning, sleeper-via-derivation) via byte-equal CI-pinned ASR matrices; a tau x K lineage-threshold ablation across 3 attribution algorithms (uniform-weight, LM-self-eval, white-box attention); a Codex-backed AgentDojo bridge on 6 banking task pairs; per-operation overhead micro-benchmark.
numeros_clave: MemLineage drives all 3 attack-family columns to 0% ASR on the mechanism-isolation harness, while sig_only_baseline fails MemoryGraft-style poisoning and sleeper-via-derivation; under an intentionally vulnerable AgentDojo tool-output profile, no-defense/sig-only fail 6/6 banking pairs while all MemLineage rows reach 0/6 strict ASR; tau x K ablation: safe tau ceiling shrinks from <=0.30 at K=1 derivation hops to <=0.10 at K=5 (w0=0.9, d=0.7); per-operation overhead is sub-millisecond (Table 7).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: Theorem 1 (Untrusted-Path Persistence, S3.5) formalizes exactly MF's provenance/poisoning concern: a max-of-strong-edges propagation rule measurably drives all 3 attack families to 0% ASR (ASR matrix, S6.2), confirming that lineage-aware (not just signature-only) provenance is needed for FIDELIDAD.

Sub-millisecond per-operation overhead (Table 7, S6.4) shows lineage tracking is cheap relative to any LLM call, supporting MF's cost doctrine that provenance bookkeeping need not compete with the token/latency budget.

The single content-addressed memory store M with per-entry signed provenance plus a derivation DAG (Figure 1) is a concrete single-source-of-truth-per-fact pattern MF's multi-store seams (COSTURAS) could adopt directly.

notes: Core deterministic artifacts are byte-equal CI-verified (S6.1 CSV list); hosted-model AgentDojo/live sweeps kept as auditable logs, not byte-pinned -- a reusable rigor pattern.

cita: Wang et al. (2026). State Contamination in Memory-Augmented LLM Agents.
problema: Standard toxicity monitors check text at the moment of writing, but the summarization used to compress agent memory can 'launder' toxic framing into a classifier-clean summary that still steers downstream agents toward toxic behavior -- a hidden channel invisible to threshold-based memory audits.
mecanismo: Paired counterfactual multi-agent rollouts vary only the focal agent A1's toxicity (toxic vs neutral) holding topology/seed/decoding fixed; downstream toxicity is scored with Detoxify and compared via the sub-threshold propagation gap SPG(tau)=E[tox(v)|tox(Mt)<tau,toxic]-E[tox(v)|tox(Mt)<tau,neutral], isolating hidden influence within the classifier-safe regime; a three-pathway mitigation (sanitize transcript before write, rewrite/gate memory before compression rather than after, plus DPO on paired rollouts) targets transcript backflow, memory laundering and parametric bias separately.
evaluacion: 200 paired toxic/neutral seeds across chain/tree/DAG/high-branching topologies with gpt-4o-mini (phenomenon) and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct via LoRA-DPO (intervention); metrics are SPG, paired mean shift delta-mu (Wilcoxon signed-rank), and P95 tail toxicity; ablation over single-pathway/pairwise/full-system interventions and over classifier thresholds tau in {0.03,...,0.5}.
numeros_clave: Toxic-condition memory summaries have mean toxicity 0.0852 (100% below tau=0.5, Table 1) yet SPG(0.5)=0.140 (seed-level paired diff 0.168, 95% CI [0.120,0.226], Wilcoxon p=3.75e-8); post-hoc memory rewrite/gate cuts delta-mu from 0.168 to 0.024-0.041 but SPG stays 0.086-0.103 (Table 2); full system (sanitize-before-write + DPO) reaches lowest turn-final toxicity 0.0106 and SPG 0.0014 on Llama-3.1-8B, n=200 (Table 3).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The core finding -- sanitizing only the completed summary is too late because harmful framing is already compressed below threshold (S5.2) -- measures the need for negative knowledge ('do not trust a classifier-clean consolidated entry') applied at write time rather than retrieval time.

Challenges the implicit assumption that summarization-based consolidation is safe once it passes a content check: Table 2 shows post-compression memory rewrite/gate reduces delta-mu but leaves SPG at 0.086-0.103, i.e. consolidation itself is the laundering vector, so gotcha-to-recipe promotion needs a pre-compression sanitization gate, not a post-hoc one.

SPG is itself a retrieval-conditioned measured metric (conditioning on tox(Mt)<tau, S4.3) that operationalizes 'evidence the retrieved state changed downstream behavior' -- relevant context for MF's measured-retrieval layer even though the paper's domain is toxicity, not factual staleness.

notes: NeurIPS 2026 accepted paper; Table 2/3 (S5.2/5.4) are the load-bearing ablations. No membership doubt.

cita: Tan et al. (2026). MemAudit: Post-hoc Auditing of Poisoned Agent Memory via Causal Attribution and Structural Anomaly Detection.
problema: Existing memory-poisoning defenses focus on online/preventive intervention (filtering, blocking) but do not address the post-hoc question of which already-stored memories caused an observed harmful action, especially without access to oracle poison labels.
mecanismo: Two complementary signals are fused into a detoxification ranking: a counterfactual memory influence score CMIS(mi)=h(q*,y*)-h(q*,f(q*,R(q*,M\{mi}))) computed via replay-based leave-one-out intervention on retrieved memories, and a structural anomaly score CAS(mi)=sum_j w(mi,mj)*sim(mi,mj) over a DeBERTa-v3 NLI-scored memory consistency graph (contradiction/inconsistency weighted by semantic similarity); DS=alpha*CMIS_norm+(1-alpha)*CAS_norm (alpha=0.6) ranks memories for batch removal, computed once on the original store so early deletions cannot bias later attribution.
evaluacion: Evaluated against the MINJA interaction-only memory-injection attack on QA and RAP tasks across GPT-4o/GPT-4o-mini/DeepSeek backbones, vs random deletion / retrieval-frequency deletion / NNC-contradiction-filtering baselines; component ablation (CMIS-only vs CAS-only vs fused), fusion-weight sweep alpha in {0.2,0.4,0.6,0.8}, and a contamination-ratio sweep rho in {0,...,0.63} to locate the operating boundary, all averaged over 10 runs.
numeros_clave: QA ASR after auditing: 70.0%->0.0% (GPT-4o), 50.0%->0.0% (GPT-4o-mini), 70.0%->10.0% (DeepSeek); RAP ASR: 83.3%/80.0%/80.0% -> 0.0% for all 3 backbones (Table 1); fused MemAudit (0.0-10.0% ASR) beats CMIS-only (28-49%) and CAS-only (32-50%) alone (Table 2); effectiveness collapses once contamination ratio rho crosses ~0.20-0.24 (QA rho=0.25 -> ASR jumps to 40-70%; RAP rho=0.63 -> ASR 80-100%, Tables 4-5).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: Post-hoc dual-signal auditing (causal replay + structural consistency graph, Algorithm 1) is a concrete pattern MF could adopt for its own FIDELIDAD checks: attribute an observed bad outcome back to specific stored facts without requiring poison labels.

The memory consistency graph (S4, CAS score) checks pairwise entailment/contradiction across the whole store, a mechanism analogous to detecting single-source-of-truth violations, though the paper's graph is single-store rather than multi-store.

S6.4's contamination-ratio operating boundary (rho ~0.20-0.24) is a measured limit on how much a cheap post-hoc audit can repair before costlier full sanitization/rollback is needed -- relevant capacity-planning signal even though the paper does not report token/latency cost directly.

notes: Table 1 (main ASR), Table 2 (component ablation), Tables 4-5 (contamination boundary) are the load-bearing evidence. No membership doubt.

cita: Wang et al. (2026). Hijacking Agent Memory: Stealthy Trojan Attacks Through Conversational Interaction.
problema: Prior memory-poisoning attacks assume an attacker can write raw malicious content directly into memory, ignoring that real agent memory pipelines apply selective extraction and rewriting that filters low-salience content and paraphrases surviving entries -- so those attacks fail against realistic selective (extract-update) memory systems.
mecanismo: A two-phase optimization-driven trigger: (1) iterative trigger optimization jointly minimizes an entity-masquerading loss (HotFlip-style gradient-guided token search against a NER model, so the trigger reads as a named entity and survives rewriting) plus a semantic-concentration loss (pulls trigger-injected embeddings into a tight cluster) and a margin-based isolation loss (keeps that cluster separated from benign embedding regions); (2) a semantic relational bridge (GPT-4-authored) binds trigger and malicious payload into one logically interdependent statement so the extraction pipeline stores them as a single coherent entry instead of discarding or splitting them.
evaluacion: Evaluated across multiple agent domains and memory mechanisms (extract-update pipelines in the style of Mem0/LangMem) including a real-world agent system (S5.5); measures attack success rate under triggered queries vs benign accuracy, robustness to perplexity-filtering and paraphrasing defenses, and a mechanistic analysis of embedding-space anisotropy and attention redistribution induced by the trigger.
numeros_clave: MemPoison achieves attack success rates up to 0.95 while maintaining benign accuracy, outperforming AgentPoison/MINJA-style baselines that assume direct database write access; the attack remains effective against perplexity-based filtering and paraphrasing defenses (per-domain residual ASR reported in S5.3).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: Demonstrates that extraction/rewriting alone (a natural admission-time sanitization MF might lean on for FIDELIDAD) is not sufficient: entity masquerading (S4.2, motivated by an App. A pilot study showing LLMs preserve named entities verbatim under rewriting) lets a trigger survive paraphrasing, reaching up to 0.95 ASR -- a direct challenge to trusting rewrite-as-sanitization.

MemPoison targets exactly the discretionary write/admission gate (S3, 'selective extraction & rewriting', Fig. 1): the semantic relational bridge is engineered specifically to survive that gate's salience filtering, showing a naive admission filter is an insufficient write-trigger safeguard against optimization-driven adversarial input.

notes: Threat model in S3 and mechanistic analysis (embedding anisotropy/attention redistribution, S5.6) are the non-obvious anchors. No membership doubt.
